newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas to spend $6 bln on downstream activities.
newsitem.headline: Petronas to spend $6 bln on downstream activities.

text.p: Malaysian state oil and gas company, Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), will spend around 15 billion ringgit ($6 billion) between now and 2000 on downstream activities, Petronas Gas Bhd managing director Abdul Rahim Abu Bakar said.

"A total of about 15 billion ringgit is expected to be expended by Petronas on downstream activites for the period beginning 1996 to the year 2000," Abdul Rahim told a natural gas conference on Monday.

He said the bulk of it would be invested in gas related activities. The capital expenditure would include around 1.3 billion ringgit for the construction of a gas pipeline, to be known as PGU III, stretching almost the entire length of the Malaysian peninsula. The project is expected to be completed by mid-1998, Abdul Rahim said.
Another 1.2 billion ringgit is expected to be spent on the construction of a second pipeline, parallel to PGU III, to be completed by 2001.

Petronas is expected to spend 3.2 billion ringgit on the construction of two gas processing plants, to be completed in 1999. Abdul Rahim said the company was also likely to invest a further 4.4 billion on "various petrochemical projects".
